1. Verify current-bill arithmetic and the total change: confirm meter reads (22,882 − 21,997 = 885 kWh), line-item sum ($18.38 + $23.29 + $118.95 = $160.62), and change versus last month ($160.62 − $226.04 = −$65.42); flag any internal mismatch as a suspected billing error.

2. Confirm price_usd and days_usd are zero: both periods fall under the same OpenEI tariff window (2025-01-01 to 2026-04-09, fixed $18.38/month, tier-1 variable $0.0263125 + $0.13441 = $0.1607225/kWh for ≤2,000 kWh), so rates are unchanged; the fixed charge is monthly and energy is billed per kWh, so the one-day difference (30 vs 31) does not change the billed amount.

3. Estimate weather_usd: use the bill history with NOAA HDD/CDD to derive a weather-to-usage relationship for heating months, isolate the weather-attributable kWh difference between last month (HDD 1,202, CDD 0) and the current period (HDD 1,069.5, CDD 0), and value those kWh at the effective variable rate (~$0.1607/kWh).

4. Compute usage_usd as the residual so price_usd + days_usd + weather_usd + usage_usd equals exactly −$65.42.

5. Screen for a billing error: reconstruct tariff-modeled totals for both periods, compare to stated totals and line items, and verify kWh against meter reads; if differences are within normal rounding, set billing_error_suspected = false and billing_error_usd = null.

6. Return only the JSON object with keys price_usd, days_usd, weather_usd, usage_usd, billing_error_suspected, and billing_error_usd.
